languageBoundary: Amber internal language only. This registry names no implementation technology and no external project, product, protocol, or research source.

method.what: Every entry's `implementation` is a measured value, not a declared intent: it records whether master's code and schemas actually carry the concept, with a file pointer for each verdict.
method.why: The superseded 1.1.0 registry marked all 49 entries `disposition: supported`. At least 12 of them have no artifact on master, and the organization-control-plane entries are contradicted directly by docs/specs/deployment-profiles.md ('purely declarative no-op'). A registry that declares support for paper contracts hides exactly the drift it exists to expose.
method.grepIsNotEvidence: Registry vocabulary and master vocabulary do not overlap, so name search both misses and misleads. `read-snapshot` has zero hits while master carries a full projection read model; `repository-registration` has zero hits while structural-identity owns `repositoryId`; `checkpoint` has many hits but means the projection read checkpoint (`--checkpoint <sha256>`) and the phase rollback checkpoint, not a sync-stream checkpoint. Every verdict below was reached by reading the named file, not by a search count.
method.supersedes: registryVersion 1.1.0 (commit 586ae63, never merged). Version domains 6 -> 3 (Slice 0); artifacts split from contracts; invariants listed as cross-cutting.

layers.contract: An interchange or read contract with a version domain. 29 entries.
layers.artifact: A canonical repository artifact family. 8 entries, crosswalked to scripts/lib/core/canonical-artifact-contracts.js TYPE_REGISTRY. No version domain: the artifact layer versions through each schema's own schemaVersion (ADR-0012).
layers.invariant: A cross-cutting constraint, not owned by any version domain. 12 entries, one per row of the baseline's invariant traceability matrix.

authorityBoundaries.note: CLAUDE.md carries the Product Boundary and Non-Goals section; governed-runner.js is the executable gate.

versionDomains.note: Absorbs the retired `source-generation` domain, which held exactly one contract and one invariant, both Core-owned. 20 entries.
SCHEMA_VERSION = 1.0.0 (scripts/lib/core/projection-registry.js:33). Absorbs the retired `component-generation` domain, which held exactly one entry. 3 entries.

retiredVersionDomains.reason: Held one contract (context-page) and one invariant; both Core-owned and already in contract-schema. Merged.
Held zero contracts. Its two invariants are cross-cutting and are listed separately.
Held one entry (projection-generation), a projection concern. Merged into projection-rule.

boundedContexts.title: Sync Runtime
boundedContexts.note: Envelope, session, admission, conflict, refusal and transport preparation are real. Subscription, cancellation settlement, reconnect and a sync-stream checkpoint are not (see the entries).

boundedContexts.title: Governed Knowledge Base
boundedContexts.note: `amber knowledge` (ADR-0009 amendment) owns the admitted record lifecycle; `amber memory` (ADR-0018) owns request/ingest/approve/book. Together they cover candidate through retired.

boundedContexts.title: Visualization Workbench
boundedContexts.note: Read-only viewer boundary per ADR-0007. The superseded registry's `read-snapshot` contract is realized here as the projection manifest plus the strict-query read surface.

boundedContexts.title: Organization Control Plane
boundedContexts.note: Only the Personal Node bootstrap exists (ADR-0019 decision D4): one deterministic local Tenant/Organization/Person scope plus a repository identity. Team, Membership, Role Assignment, Policy Assignment and administrative fencing have no master artifact, and docs/specs/deployment-profiles.md states the declared profile selects no runtime behavior. 3 of its 9 contracts are implemented, in bootstrap form only.

entries.title: Sync Envelope
entries.note: Carries envelopeId, artifactRef {path, hash}, a required scope {tenantId, repositoryId, repositoryGeneration}, profile, and versionNegotiation {amberProtocolVersion, minCompatibleVersion, capabilities}.

nearMisses.why: The graph has a closed six-verb edge vocabulary and a node set derived from pages, artifacts and wiki documents, but no fact type.
Session telemetry over a session's own stages, not a canonical domain fact-change event.

entries.title: Sync Control Record
entries.note: None of the control-plane concerns the Sync Runtime owns in the baseline — subscription, cancellation settlement, reconnect — has a master artifact.

nearMisses.why: A transport preparation report (mode is always `prepare`). Synchronization telemetry, not a control record.

entries.title: Sync Session
entries.note: Session record is {sessionId, operation, startedAt, status, target}. Its ledgers live under .amber/sync/ (applied.jsonl, refused.jsonl, conflicts.jsonl). CLI surface: amber sync session <run|push|pull|list|replay|conflicts|approve|ledger>.

entries.title: Sync Operation
entries.note: The preparation-side shape is implemented: a closed verb set with confined paths or a derived commit message, never a shell string. The operation lifecycle — cancellation settlement, reconnect — is not implemented; see sync-control-record.

entries.title: Checkpoint
entries.nameCollision: The word `checkpoint` names two unrelated master mechanisms: the projection read checkpoint `amber projection strict-query --checkpoint <sha256>` (derived from the projection's canonical source set) and `amber phase rollback --checkpoint <id>`. Neither is the sync-stream checkpoint this entry means, and neither resumes a sync.

nearMisses.why: The ADR-0029 section 8.1 session lease fence (a request carrying an older fence can never settle). Stage-run ownership, a different domain from sync-runtime ownership handoff.

entries.title: Conflict
entries.note: CONFLICT_TYPES closes at four: concurrent-edit, generation-mismatch, version-mismatch, identity-mismatch. Recorded append-only in .amber/sync/conflicts.jsonl.

entries.title: Resolution
entries.note: RESOLUTIONS closes at four: pending, local-wins, remote-wins, manual-merge-required. Resolution is recorded and governed, never auto-applied — every refusal preserves the local artifact (`local artifact preserved`).

entries.title: Rejection
entries.note: Refusal is a first-class ledger family, not an error path: markEnvelopeRefused writes .amber/sync/refused.jsonl. Semantic refusals carry a conflict type; path/type/schema violations return status `invalid` instead.

entries.title: Corruption
entries.note: A local artifact whose sha256 differs from the envelope's artifactRef.hash is refused as concurrent-edit and the local artifact is preserved (sync-remote.js:401). There is no separately-named Corruption contract; the concern is covered by the refusal paths.

entries.title: Read Snapshot
entries.note: The capability is real and is what the workbench reads, but the identifier is not registered: master exposes it as the rebuildable projection manifest (SCHEMA_VERSION 1.0.0) plus strict-query. A peer presenting `read-snapshot` gets no match, hence compatibility `unknown`.

entries.title: Query Contract
entries.note: Exact scope, checkpoint, projection version, limit, sort, depth and an expiring cursor are all required parameters; an unknown scope is denied and a stale dependency is refused. The knowledge side adds an exact-scope `amber knowledge query --scope` where an unknown scope is denied.

entries.title: Projection Query Envelope
entries.note: Master splits this into the strict-query parameter contract (amber projection strict-query --scope --checkpoint --projection-version --limit --sort --depth [--cursor]) and the read-receipt record that closes the read. There is no wrapper artifact carrying the name.

entries.title: Projection Read Receipt
entries.note: recordReadReceipt({scope, projectionType, resultHash}) writes the receipt; verifyReceipt(receiptId) re-derives it. listReadReceipts is the read path.

entries.title: Knowledge Candidate
entries.note: The candidate stage is the memory request at .amber/memory/requests/<requestId>.json (trigger, conversion, escape-hatch and ratification channels). `amber memory ingest` mechanically admits request entries into the registry as proposals; `amber memory approve` is the entry-level human review gate.

entries.title: Knowledge Record
entries.note: Lifecycle closes at draft/proposal/active/superseded/needs-re-review/abandoned — the baseline's candidate/review/accepted/stale/refresh-required/superseded/retired in master vocabulary. The ADR-0009 amendment is real: `amber knowledge admit --page <id>` admits a record from a canonical Context Page, and `amber knowledge status` reports fresh/stale.

entries.title: Context Page
entries.note: Reassigned from the retired `source-generation` domain, which held this one contract plus one invariant. Both were Core-owned, so the domain carried no distinct version surface.

entries.title: Projection Generation
entries.note: Reassigned from the retired `component-generation` domain, which held exactly this entry. PROJECTION_TYPES closes at governance-graph, knowledge-base, visualization-workbench; rebuild regenerates from canonical state and drift is reported by projectionStatus.

entries.title: Person Identity
entries.note: Bootstrap only (ADR-0019 decision D4): personId resolves from .amber/identity.json, else git config user.name/user.email, else null. There is no admission step, no cross-repository Person, and no authority beyond the local administrative scope.

nearMisses.why: `agentId` is a declared field on every resolved identity that resolveIdentity sets to null unconditionally. The slot exists; the identity type does not.

entries.title: Tenant and Organization Structure
entries.note: One deterministic local scope — DEFAULT_TENANT_ID 'local' and DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_ID 'personal' — overridable per field by .amber/identity.json, and carried on every envelope as a required scope. There is no multi-tenant structure, no Tenant lifecycle, and no nesting.

entries.title: Team
entries.nameCollision: `amber team` is a deprecated verb that inspects local team-distribution metadata and is marked for removal in v2 — unrelated to Organization Control Plane teams. Separately, the `team-hub` deployment profile is a declarative label: docs/specs/deployment-profiles.md states its only runtime consumer is the provenance stamp on sync envelopes.

nearMisses.why: The F050 principal snapshot carries a `membership` field. That registry is repository-local approval authority (PRINCIPAL_SNAPSHOT_FIELDS in approval-registry.js:139), not tenant-wide Organization Control Plane membership.

entries.title: Repository Registration
entries.note: The superseded registry listed this among the zero-hit contracts; that was a grep miss. resolveRepositoryId derives a stable identity from .amber/identity.json, else the git remote, else a bootstrap default, and never from the directory name. repositoryGeneration plus transferRecord carry the fenced-transfer record — at schema level only; enforcement does not exist (see administrative-fencing).

nearMisses.why: `amber principal register --role` assigns a repository-local approval role validated against a closed field set. The baseline's Role Assignment is tenant-wide and belongs to the Organization Control Plane, which does not exist.

Deny-wins command policy (F050, `amber policy`) is evaluated against the target repository's .amber/governance/rules.json and gates repository-local work. Assigning a policy to an organization role, and the org-wide deny-wins ceiling the baseline requires, do not exist.
transferRecord records a tenant transfer and its previousGeneration. It is a record, not a fence: nothing enforces that a transferred repository starts with no target-Tenant authorization.
leaseFence guards stage-run settlement against a stale owner. A different fence in a different plane.

entries.title: Work Artifact
entries.note: The baseline's 'canonical work' is master's committed canonical artifact revision store under .amber/artifacts/<type>/<identity-slug>/, with a type registry, lifecycle states, traces and a committed-only visibility rule. `work` is not a master type name.

entries.title: Decision Artifact
entries.masterConcept: Decision (canonical artifact type + ledger Decision primitive)
entries.note: TYPE_REGISTRY.decision, state `recorded` only, requiring exactly one `decides` trace onto a committed artifact revision. Admission binds the acting Principal verified against the registry.

entries.title: Evidence Artifact
entries.note: Evidence discipline per ADR-0004. The web surface consumes the same records through apps/web/server/services/evidence-jobs.ts.

entries.title: Approval Artifact
entries.note: Append-only event ledger under .amber/principals/ protected by a tamper-evident hash chain: a fold over an edited ledger fails closed as corruption. Each event binds the previous event's hash; there is no in-place mutation path.

entries.title: Context Artifact
entries.masterConcept: Context Page / Context Request / Context Loadout
entries.note: ADR-0009/ADR-0010. The context page is simultaneously the Core form of the Knowledge Record lifecycle (see the knowledge-record contract).

entries.title: Learning Artifact
entries.note: Reached through `amber learnings`, which inspects whether accepted work hit a knowledge write-back trigger and books the review under --reviewed.

entries.title: Ledger Artifact
entries.note: Append-only lineage with a hash chain, per ADR-0004. Written through the governed runner so a mutation cannot bypass the ledger gate.

entries.title: Acceptance Artifact
entries.masterConcept: Acceptance entry in the evolution log
entries.note: `amber accept` appends the entry, sets the plan's own Status field to accepted, and updates feature_list.json only when the feature is not already accepted. It is fail-closed: a refusal writes nothing.

entries.title: Repository-local authority
entries.note: The baseline asks ADR-0001 to distinguish repository-local Core from optional non-executing distributed contexts. ADR-0001 is present and the product boundary in CLAUDE.md states the distinction; the amendment itself is not visible as a separate ADR revision.

entries.title: Offline operation
entries.note: Amber state is repository-local and every read path is a local file read. The sync runtime shells out to git only and never opens a network connection of its own.

entries.title: Optional non-executing Sync Runtime
entries.note: The sync surface is opt-in and the transport report's mode is always `prepare`: proposedOps are structured verbs, never shell strings, and Amber never executes them. The one governed local sync commit rides ADR-0003's narrow exception (ADR-0020 Stage A) under single-use human approval.

entries.title: One versioned protocol and artifact model
entries.note: ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION and the envelope's versionNegotiation block carry amberProtocolVersion, minCompatibleVersion and a closed capability list. checkCompatibility refuses a newer major and refuses a silent downgrade below minCompatibleVersion. Schema versioning runs through the single schema-contract seam.

entries.title: Rebuildable read-only projections
entries.note: `amber projection rebuild` regenerates from canonical state at any time and projectionStatus reports missing/current/drifted. ADR-0007's supervised read-only viewer boundary is preserved.

entries.title: Exact-scope deny-wins authorization and privacy minimization
entries.note: Deny-wins evaluation over .amber/governance/rules.json with defaultAction=deny is real and repository-local, with an explicit minimization marker on retention events. The organization-wide exact-scope authorization the baseline pairs with it does not exist, because the Organization Control Plane does not.

entries.title: Fail-closed degraded read-only
entries.note: A corrupt projection source makes the source unreadable rather than the projection partial: the artifact half of the governance-graph source is read through the strictly read-only listArtifactRevisions seam so corruption fails closed. Corrupt or missing governance state is a blocker, never an empty state.

entries.title: Append-only lineage and immutable records
entries.note: jsonl ledgers are append-only and hash-chained; `amber phase transitions` exposes the append-only lineage and `amber phase rollback` is explicitly non-destructive. The principal registry carries no in-place mutation path.

entries.title: Source and Resolution ownership
entries.masterConcept: Context Page as the Core form of the Knowledge Record
entries.note: The amendment the baseline asks for is implemented: `amber knowledge admit --page <id> --auth <authorization>` admits a Knowledge Record from a canonical Context Page, so the page keeps source ownership and the record owns resolution.

entries.title: Conflict preservation and governed resolution
entries.note: Conflicts are recorded in an append-only ledger and every refusal that concerns an existing local artifact preserves it, so resolution is a governed human act (manual-merge-required) rather than an automatic overwrite.

entries.title: Tenant and Repository isolation
entries.masterConcept: Structural isolation on the envelope scope
entries.note: Isolation is structural, not policy-level: the envelope scope {tenantId, repositoryId, repositoryGeneration} is required, and admitEnvelope compares identity before any artifact content is read or hashed, refusing a foreign tenant, repository or generation.

entries.title: No hidden authority or execution
entries.masterConcept: Governed execution gates, no hidden authority
entries.note: Every mutation returns through the governed runner's ledger, policy, confidence, approval and worktree gates. ADR-0005 removed execution authority; ADR-0003's narrow governed exception is preserved and ADR-0020 Stage A rides it. No context intercepts tools, dispatches workers, or executes target-repository work.

compatibility.note: This matrix is a declaration over the three surviving version domains. It is not the runtime check: checkCompatibility() in scripts/lib/core/sync-remote.js compares a single minCompatibleVersion scalar per envelope and refuses a newer major or a silent downgrade. A domain-level combination matrix has no runtime counterpart, and this registry does not add one.

entryRollup.note: Per-entry compatibility is derived from measured implementation: `supported` exactly when the concept exists on master, `unknown` otherwise (an unregistered identifier fails closed). The 12 unknown entries are the superseded registry's false 'supported' claims: 11 designed-not-implemented contracts plus the superseded read-snapshot.

cases.description: All three version domains are at their current supported versions.
All three version domains are in their declared deprecated ranges.
All three version domains are in their declared refused ranges.
The Runtime Protocol version is not registered, so the combination fails closed as unknown.
